title: Show it, do not hand it out
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Is your information easy to see or hard to read?

Jose showed a spreadsheet of property prices, rents and sales, and asked what the challenges are. A student said that it is hard to separate and visualize. Jose said it is intimidating, and bar graphs make it easier.
Another student said that visuals allow you to come to determinations quicker, because the information is easier to see.
Jose said that for a daily sales report he asked for a visual of how ten people performed each day, and that the more visual the better, especially for presentations.
Jose said that people have a tolerance for time, so you must plan your story to fit it.
He said that rookies hand the presentation out to everybody at the meeting, so everyone reads ahead and stops listening to you.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you would draw it as a graph.
Write how long people will stay with you.
Write what you will hand out after, not before.
Write the one picture that says it.

check.q: What did Jose say makes a spreadsheet easier to read?
What did a student say visuals allow?
What did Jose say rookies do?
choices: Hand out the presentation at the start

recap: Show pictures. Respect people's time. Hand out later.
